obligations.statement: One accepted refresh atomically consumes the old token and installs exactly one fresh token.
evidence: canonical bounded Rust auth state model
assumptions: the database transaction provides the isolation required by the refresh-consumption update

obligations.statement: A consumed or non-current refresh token is rejected without mutating the session.
evidence: canonical bounded Rust auth state model
assumptions: token digests preserve equality and collision resistance at the application boundary

obligations.statement: After logout, expiry, or administrative revocation no refresh or access token can reactivate the session.
evidence: canonical bounded Rust auth state model
assumptions: revocation reads observe authoritative PostgreSQL state

obligations.statement: Signing-key rotation preserves an explicit overlap window, keeps the active key trusted, and rejects tokens after their signing key is retired.
evidence: canonical bounded Rust auth state model
assumptions: key identifiers uniquely select the intended verification key

obligations.statement: External accounts are linked only by configured authority, tenant, and provider subject—not email equality.
assumptions: provider subject and issuer verification are trustworthy

obligations.statement: Accepted and issued JWTs enforce the configured issuer, audience, algorithm, expiry, not-before, signing key, and session provenance.
evidence: JWKS algorithm and key allow-list tests
assumptions: cryptographic libraries satisfy their documented contracts
JWKS transport supplies authentic configured key material
